🇸🇦🇾🇪 Joe Kent: Sending Syrian fighters to Yemen could create an even bigger threat to Saudi Arabia

Reports that Syria could send troops to help Saudi Arabia fight the Houthis have Joe Kent seriously concerned.

And his argument is worth paying attention to.

Syria's President Ahmed al-Sharaa has a problem. His military includes battle-hardened jihadist factions and foreign fighters who could eventually threaten his own government.

Kent believes sending some of those fighters to Yemen might look like a convenient solution. Sharaa gets rid of potential rivals, Saudi Arabia gets reinforcements, and Washington avoids another direct military commitment.

But there's a dangerous catch.

Yemen is already home to Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula, one of the group's most dangerous branches. Kent fears that sending experienced Syrian militants into the country could strengthen AQAP rather than defeat the Houthis.

And the consequences might eventually reach Saudi Arabia itself.

He warns that a stronger jihadist network in Yemen could revive Al-Qaeda's ambitions to threaten Mecca and Medina.

It's the kind of short-term calculation Washington has made before: backing armed groups against one enemy, only to discover that those groups become a much bigger problem later.

Kent's warning is that Syria could end up exporting its extremist problem to Yemen, only for Saudi Arabia and the United States to inherit an even more dangerous one.
